X is $CH_3CH=CH–O–C(CH_3)=CH_2$, a divinyl ether. Under mild acid, each half is released as an enol that tautomerises to a carbonyl compound.
First half: $CH_3CH=CH–OH \rightarrow CH_3CH_2CHO$ (propanal, Y), $M = 58\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$.
Second half: $CH_2=C(CH_3)OH \rightarrow CH_3COCH_3$ (acetone, Z), $M = 58\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$.
(A) Y and Z are both $C_3H_6O$, so their molar masses are equal. Correct.
(B) Neither compound is acidic enough to react with $NaHCO_3$, so it cannot distinguish them. Incorrect.
(C) The aldehyde is less hindered and more electrophilic, so propanal adds HCN faster than acetone. Incorrect.
(D) Both carbonyls add 2,4-DNP (addition followed by elimination) to give 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazones. Correct.
Only A and D are correct.
Answer: (D) A and D only
